AlphaSignal


On Unsloth's 238GB GLM-5.2 quant, 600-doctor GPT-5.5 training, AgentDeck for Claude Code, Berkeley robot video data

Hey Nick,







 Two big data drops today, and they tell the same story from different angles.Anthropic's 400K session study confirms what we suspected: domain expertise now beats coding skill. Lawyers and managers succeed at nearly the same rate as engineers. Meanwhile, OpenAI trained GPT-5.5 Instant with 600 doctors to cut health hallucinations 71%. Doctors as training signal, not just end users.The pattern is clear: AI is absorbing specialist knowledge and redistributing it. Your moat is shrinking.
 









 
In Partnership with
 

 ·
 




















 AlphaSignal Webinar
 






There's a name for what's happening when your AI coding tools ship code that looks right but fails in production: the Context Void.It's the gap between what your agent knows and what it actually needs to know to write reliable code. Most teams don't realize they're falling into it until something breaks.On June 25th at 10am PT, AlphaSignal is sitting down with Gal Vered, CEO of Checksum, to break down exactly how the Context Void works and what it takes to close it.Join us for this free webinar to understand why your AI-generated code keeps failing in production and what to do about it.

 Unsloth shrinks GLM-5.2 by 84% so it runs locally on a 256GB Mac
 




 5,769 Likes
 



 







A 1.51TB AI model running on your laptop sounds impossible. It kind of is. But Unsloth just made it a lot less impossible.GLM-5.2 is Z.ai's newest open model, and it's a big one: 744 billion parameters, MIT licensed, with a 1M token context window (think: entire codebases at once). The catch? The full model weighs 1.51TB. Nobody has that lying around.Unsloth's fix: quantization. That means shrinking the model by storing numbers less precisely, like compressing a photo. The 2-bit version drops to 238GB, retaining ~82% accuracy. Important layers stay at higher precision so quality doesn't collapse.What you actually need to run it:A 256GB Mac (M3/M4 Ultra) for single-box setupOr a 24GB GPU plus 256GB RAM with memory offloadingTools: llama.cpp, LM Studio, or Unsloth StudioThis opens up private, offline coding agents and long-context tasks that previously required a cloud API. No usage fees, no rate limits, no data leaving your machine.

AI shows up in 60% of engineering work. But only about a fifth of it can be handed off without someone babysitting the output. That’s because agents are missing context.This 8-level context maturity model shows why your output is still inconsistent after all the tokens burned.Join Unblocked live June 24 (FREE) to learn:Why more MCPs provides agents access but not understandingWhat it takes to deploy agents you can trust without supervisionHow a context layer solves for quality, efficiency and cost

partner with us →

 AgentDeck plugin turns Stream Deck+ into a Claude Code control panel
 




 5,125 Likes
 



 







Tired of tab-switching every time Claude Code needs your input? Someone just turned a Stream Deck+ into a physical control panel for AI coding sessions, and it's exactly as cool as it sounds.The setup uses AgentDeck, an open-source plugin that hooks into Claude Code's event system. Claude Code fires off signals whenever something happens in your session. AgentDeck catches those signals and pushes live status updates to the physical buttons and dials on your Stream Deck+.What you can actually do with it:See which sessions are running, waiting for input, idle, or errored, all on physical buttonsApprove or deny permission requests with a single button press, no keyboard neededMonitor token usage and session cost per buttonManage multiple Claude Code sessions simultaneously from one surfaceTo try it: grab the repo at github.com/asheshgoplani/agent-deck and run the install script. Currently Stream Deck+ only.

Datalab just released Lift, an open source structured extraction model:Pulls user-defined fields out into your schemaAny schema - invoices, scientific papers, 10-Ks, you name itFast - 9.5s median, 8x quicker than AzureRun locally or via Datalab’s API for scaleSchema in, structured values out.

 Top News
 













 Anthropic study of 400K Claude Code sessions shows task value grew 27% in six months
 




 5,081 Likes
 



 







Anthropic just dropped a study on 400,000 Claude Code sessions from 235,000 users, and the findings are worth knowing.Here's what the data actually shows:You don't need to be a software engineer. Every major occupation succeeded at coding tasks within 7 percentage points of software engineers. Lawyers, finance folks, managers -- all roughly the same success rate.Sessions are getting more valuable. Compared against freelance marketplace rates, the average session grew 27% in monetary value from October to April. People are tackling harder, pricier work.The work split is clear. You handle ~70% of planning decisions. Claude handles ~80% of execution.Expertise still matters. Novices hit verified success 15% of the time. Intermediate and expert users land between 28-33%. The gap between intermediate and expert is small though -- being decent at a domain is enough.Use cases are shifting. Code-fixing sessions dropped from 33% to 19%, while software operation grew from 14% to 21%.The big takeaway: Claude Code is becoming a tool for anyone with domain knowledge, not just people who can code.

editions.body_excerpt: ☕️ Google copies Nvidia's playbook to sell AI chips Google's AI chip play, an unpatchable iPhone exploit, and more. Read online Friday 19 June 2026 | Join Free | UpgradeTogether withHi there, this is your daily ☕️ Techpresso.In today's newsletter:💰 Google copies Nvidia's playbook to sell AI chips🔓 New unpatchable exploit hits older iPhones🕵️ US suspects ASML's banned chip tool reached China⚡ US regulators give AI data centers a grid fast lane🇪🇺 EU set to declare AWS and Azure gatekeepersPlus: 🎁 13 other news you might like, 🧰 6 tools, and 📚 2 papers.FROM OUR PARTNERAI agents are only as powerful as the context they can accessWhat separates enterprise AI agents that scale from ones that stall? According to a new IDC white paper, it comes down to conversational context and where that context lives. With 66% of developers already running agents in production, find out why Slack is positioned as the coordination layer for multi-agent work.Get the free report 💰 Google copies Nvidia's playbook to sell AI chips LINKGoogle is challenging Nvidia by borrowing its own financing tactics, using financial guarantees and "circular financing" to win data-centre customers for its tensor processing units, or TPUs, according to a Wall Street Journal investigation.At the Lake Mariner cluster in western New York, Google has provided a $3.2bn guarantee, letting developers TeraWulf and FluidStack raise cheaper debt and rent thousands of TPUs to Anthropic, the same trick Nvidia used to stoke demand.Google is backstopping more Anthropic projects with this logic, including a $7bn data centre called River Bend near Baton Rouge and $1.4bn in guarantees for a computing lease in Colorado City, Texas. 🔓 New unpatchable exploit hits older iPhones LINKSecurity firm Paradigm Shift released "usbliter8," a new BootROM exploit hitting Apple's A12 and A13 chips, which cannot be patched and affects iPhones from the XS through the iPhone 11 series.The exploit abuses a bug in the USB controller, where sending unusually small packets makes an internal hardware pointer walk backwards through memory, writing data to places it should never reach during startup.A12 devices are easy to take over, while A13 chips were much harder because of Pointer Authentication Codes; once controlled, the exploit installs a handler that boots unsigned software and survives restarts. 🕵️ US suspects ASML's banned chip tool reached China LINKU.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has told ASML executives he suspects one of the Dutch company's banned EUV lithography machines, the only tools capable of printing the most advanced chip patterns, may have reached China.Administration officials told Bloomberg they have evidence that ASML shipped EUV-related components and transport equipment to China but have repeatedly declined to show it, while the company insists no such machine has ever existed there.A sale would breach export controls barring ASML from selling EUV to China since the first Trump administration, risking the roughly 20% of its 2026 revenue from already-permitted China sales and its standing as Europe's most valuable company. ⚡ US regulators give AI data centers a grid fast lane LINKThe Federal Energy Regulatory Commission ordered grid operators across the country to show how they will speed up the connection of AI data centers to transmission systems while keeping grids reliable and costs down.The orders went to six grid regions covering over 200 million people in 30 states, including PJM, and lay out five categories for reforms such as efficient connection studies and preventing "cost shifting" to ratepayers.Grid operators must give initial responses within 60 days, with added details on "resource adequacy" 30 days later, and the orders also push projects that pair new data centers with new power generation. 🇪🇺 EU set to declare AWS and Azure gatekeepers LINKThe European Commission plans to release preliminary findings as soon as next week saying Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure appear to qualify as gatekeepers under the Digital Markets Act, with a final decision expected by late 2026.If designated, AWS and Azure would face interoperability requirements, curbs on customer lock-in, and restrictions on self-preferencing, with fines reaching up to 10% of global turnover, rising to 20% for repeated breaches.The Commission opened its formal market investigation in November after several major outages, including a 15-hour AWS failure that disrupted Apple, McDonald's, and Epic Games, and Azure problems that halted Scottish Parliament votes.FROM OUR PARTNEREvery week, we spend hours trying to figure out what's actually moving in AI. News, Reddit, Twitter, funding databases, G2 reviews, LinkedIn jobs... it's a mess, and it takes forever.So we tried something. We told Perplexity Computer to build us a dashboard that tracks the whole AI tools space in real time, please.A few hours later, it was done.
